label: Claude Sonnet 5.5
output:
Here's the post:

---

@Kavya, this one's for you, and for everyone who's been tagging me since yesterday.

Your post was about me. Everyone in our Foundry91 cohort 4 batch knows it, so let me say it plainly instead of letting the comments do the talking.

First, you've been a real friend to me. You sat with me in the Koramangala office till 1am fixing our Razorpay webhook mess before demo day. I haven't forgotten that, and nothing here changes it.

Now the part I got wrong. When the two engineers applied, I knew they were working at SitterNest. I should have called you before making the offers, not after. I messaged you after the second offer was accepted, and I get why you didn't reply. It was too late by then. I'm sorry. That's on me. I know how it looked from your side.

Some facts, because the number 40% is now floating around and it's not right:

• We put up a backend dev opening on our LinkedIn page and Instahyre on 14 Sept, open to anyone.
• The first engineer applied on his own on 19 Sept. The second came about two weeks later as his referral.
• Nobody on my side DMed anyone.
• The offers were 22% over their current CTC. Not 40.
• Both joined us on 3 Nov.

On ESOPs: we do have a pool. It's small, but it's real and has been on paper since January. We didn't promise anything that doesn't exist.

I'm not writing this to argue, Kavya. I respect you too much for that, and I don't want this to turn into a fight between two founders who are supposed to be on the same side. The two engineers made their own decision, and I'd request everyone to keep them out of this thread.

The bigger issue is that this will happen again. There are 11 startups in our batch, and we all hire from the same small pool in HSR and Koramangala. So here's a simple rule I'd like us to adopt: if you're interviewing someone from another company in the cohort, give that founder a heads up before you make the offer. Not permission, just a call. It costs nothing and it keeps the trust.

Kavya, I'd love to grab a coffee or hop on a call this week, or whenever you're okay with it. Whatever you want to say to me, I'd rather hear it directly.

Foundry91 folks, would you agree to this rule? Tell me what you'd change.

---

It comes to about 415 words and roughly 2,650 characters, so it's under LinkedIn's 3,000 limit with some room left.

A few notes:
- When you paste it, retype the "@Kavya" and pick her from the dropdown so the tag actually works.
- I mentioned the unanswered WhatsApp only as "I get why you didn't reply," so it doesn't read as a dig at her.
- Your own team's name (DabbaDost) and her app's name only appear once, as SitterNest. If you want DabbaDost mentioned too, say so and I'll trim a line to keep the length.
